newsitem.title: USA: United Stationers looks at oper expenses.
newsitem.headline: United Stationers looks at oper expenses.

text.p: United Stationers Inc said Wednesday it sees room for further improvement in its operating expenses, which were 12.1 percent of net sales in 1996.

Citing the benefits of the company's merger activity, chief financial officer Dan Bushell said, "Operating expenses have periodically dipped below 12 percent. We believe there is further room for (operating efficiency) improvement, primarily through warehouse and system efficiencies and greater sales leverage," he added in a statement.
On a reclassified basis, the company also reported gross margin percentage for 1996 was 17 percent compared with 17.4 percent in 1995.
Earlier, United Stationers, an office products wholesaler, reported record fourth-quarter earnings of $0.63 a diluted share on 9.1 percent higher sales of $599.3 million.
